events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Washington County in north central Kansas...
Northern Marshall County in northeastern Kansas...
Northern Nemaha County in northeastern Kansas...

* WHEN...Until 400 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1236 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1.5 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Marysville, Sabetha, Seneca, Axtell, Greenleaf, Beattie, Bern,
Barnes, Oneida and Baileyville.

events.summary:
Corrected wave height.

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 4 PM CHST SATURDAY...
...HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SATURDAY
AFTERNOON...

* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 9 to 12 feet and dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...West, north and east facing reefs of Guam and Rota.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As TY In-fa moves through the far northern
CNMI, the large, long-period northeast to north swell emanating
from In-fa will maintain hazardous surf along north and east
facing reefs. Seas have begun to slowly subside and will
gradually turn northwest, ending hazardous surf along east
facing reefs and beginning hazardous surf along west facing
reefs this evening. Surf will remain hazardous through
Saturday afternoon. These surf conditions will maintain a high
risk of dangerous rip currents. Although surf will fall below
hazardous levels along east facing reefs, the rip current risk
will remain high.

events.summary:
FFWTOP

The National Weather Service in Topeka has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Marshall County in northeastern Kansas...

* Until 415 AM CDT.

* At 1215 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beattie.

* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...South Central De Baca County in east central New Mexico...
Northern Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 115 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable. River or stream flows
are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1112 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central De Baca and Northern Chaves
Counties.
- Elevated flows are expected in the Pecos River. Stay away from
riverbanks.
